THE ADJUDICATION AXIS IS DERIVABLE-vs-RECALL, NOT PART A vs PART B.
DERIVABLE — Part A, plus any Part B item settled by science, a textbook
statement, or the stem's own words. The derivation wins where it is
decisive, whatever the keys say. Q70 is the clean case: it is arithmetic.
RECALL — history, polity, current affairs, defence exercises. Defer to the
keys where they AGREE. Where they split and our own pass was LOW, the row
is UNRESOLVED and is not applied at all.

outcome.note: 21 rows where the three sources do not all agree: the original 16, plus 5 where our answer matched Dreamers and Centurion alone dissents.

keepOurs.class: SELF-REFUTING — and we depart from BOTH keys here
keepOurs.why: THE ONE ROW WHERE WE OVERRIDE A UNANIMOUS EXTERNAL VERDICT, so it is stated plainly. The stem asks which group of LANDLOCKED states borders Madhya Pradesh. MP's five neighbours are Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Gujarat — and Maharashtra and Gujarat both have a coastline. Option A is all five, i.e. it answers 'which states border MP' and drops the stem's own qualifier. The option set is built to test exactly that qualifier: A ignores 'landlocked', B and C wrongly add Jharkhand (which does NOT border MP, Chhattisgarh separates them), D is the three landlocked ones. Two keys agreeing on A is consistent with two key-setters making the same highly available mistake — the correlated-error limit this project documents elsewhere. No amount of agreement makes Gujarat landlocked. Worth a human sanity-check precisely because it is unanimous against us.

Re-derived rather than voted on. 252-250 = 2 g of steam condensed. Heat absorbed by the original water = 250 x 1 x (25-20) = 1250 Cal. Heat released = latent heat of condensation plus the cooling of that condensate from 100 to 25 = 2L + 2 x 1 x 75. Balancing, 2L = 1100 and L = 550 Cal/g, which is option C. No self-consistent reading of the stem returns Centurion's 560. A calculation is not a matter for majority vote.

Statement III is the false one and Centurion's 'all three' requires it to be true. NCERT Class 11 Physical Geography has the wind blowing PARALLEL to the isobars once the pressure-gradient and Coriolis forces balance; III asserts the opposite. I and II are both near-verbatim from the same chapter, including II's 'directly proportional to the angle of latitude', which is the book's own wording.

The stem asks which statements are NOT correct. II is false (soapstone is talc, the softest mineral on the Mohs scale, so granite is harder, not softer) and IV is false (foliation is a METAMORPHIC feature, not a sedimentary one), giving II and IV = C. Centurion's B would require rocks not to be aggregates of minerals and gabbro not to be black, both of which the same chapter states outright.

All three statements are items from the standard list of functions of political parties. Centurion's B excludes I — that in most democracies elections are fought mainly among party candidates — which is the first function the chapter lists.

flippedToOurs.why: REVERSED. Pair II is the textbook exclamatory transformation and is correct. Pair I keeps 'here' where reported speech shifts it to 'there', so it is not correctly stated — giving 'II only'. The first pass deferred on the explicit reasoning that 'the key is the only external signal' for a question of convention. That premise is now false: there are two signals, they disagree, and the one agreeing with the mechanical rule also agrees with our derivation. Nothing in the stem establishes that speaker and reporter share a place, which is the only reading under which retaining 'here' is defensible.

REVERSED, and recorded as genuinely contested. C is false (a uniform massive rope has tension varying along its length) and D is false (the heavier side descends, so the centre of mass accelerates), so the answer is A or B and the two differ only in how 'same acceleration' is read. Under a scalar reading the inextensibility constraint gives every point the same magnitude of acceleration, which is A and is the standard result taught at this level; under a strict vector reading the two sides accelerate in opposite directions, which is B. The first pass asserted that B was 'plainly what the item is testing' — an assertion, not evidence. Against it: our blind pass derived A and named B as the runner-up under exactly the vector reading, the second key says A, and a vector subtlety is out of character for a paper pitched at this level, where the distinctive physics is that tension is NOT uniform. A rigorous reading still favours B, so this is the row in the set most worth a second opinion.

REVERSED. The Ramanujan Fellowship is a DST fellowship for returning researchers, and the Anusandhan National Research Foundation is the body that now houses DST's research-funding schemes. The Research, Development and Innovation Fund is a financing corpus aimed at private-sector deep-tech R&D, not a home for an individual fellowship. The first pass deferred to a lone key on a recall row; the second key agrees with our derivation and with the substantive reading.

REVERSED. Vayu Shakti is the IAF firepower demonstration held at the Pokhran range in Jaisalmer district, so I is correct, and Apache and Chinook are both in IAF service and routinely feature, so III is correct. The only doubt our deriver raised was whether Mirage 2000 took part, which is what would drop II and yield Dreamers' answer — but the upgraded Mirage 2000 remains in service and is a standing participant. All three correct.

REVERSED, and it is settleable after all — the first pass recorded it as unsettleable from the page and deferred. River Basin Management is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti, so I is true; the Brahmaputra Board is a statutory body under the same ministry and an implementing agency for its basin, so III is true; and the scheme's objectives are integrated basin planning, flood management and inter-state river data, NOT promoting water for domestic use, so II is the planted false statement. Dreamers' C requires I false and II true, which inverts both.

acceptKeys.why: Both keys agree, and D was our deriver's own named runner-up. School colloid tables routinely list foam rubber under 'Foam' rather than distinguishing solid foam, so the examiner counts all four pairs matched.

Both keys agree, so the deference rule applies — but this remains the most uncomfortable of them and is left flagged. The stem scopes itself to respiration in ANIMALS, and in animals anaerobic respiration yields lactic acid with no CO2, which would make statement III true and our 'I and III' right. The keys' 'I only' is the yeast/fermentation reading, which the stem's own scope excludes. Our deriver named this tension in advance and called it its least secure item in the range. Deferring on unanimity, not because the keys are clearly right.

Both keys agree. Statement II dates the blast furnace to the beginning of the 18th century, matching the standard narrative of Darby's coke-smelting blast furnace of 1709 that Industrial-Revolution chapters teach. Recall item.

Both keys agree and our own pass was LOW, stating outright that it held nothing about the March 2026 uranium agreement — not the parties, not the figure — and that India-Australia and India-Canada were both live and inseparable. Keys win; this is what LOW is for.

Both keys agree and our own pass was LOW, holding neither the host States nor the mascot of the inaugural Khelo India Tribal Games, and taking all three statements rather than manufacture a falsehood.

unresolved.why: DO NOT APPLY without external verification. The two keys SPLIT, and our own pass is not a third voice: it was LOW and said in its own note that it does not hold IBCA membership as of 2026 and chose France on a range-state pattern argument alone. A guess agreeing with a key is not corroboration. The question needs the actual International Big Cat Alliance membership list; everything else here is inference.

DO NOT APPLY without external verification. Statement I is securely false (the Goldman Environmental Prize is annual, not biennial) and statement II is structurally safe (the prize gives six awards a year, one per region, so one winner is always from Asia). Everything turns on III — whether all six 2026 winners are women — which decides between our B and Centurion's D. Our pass was LOW and reasoned from a prior rather than from knowledge of the 2026 slate, so although ours and Dreamers agree, that is one piece of evidence and a guess, not two.
